newsitem.title: USA: Detroit mayor calls for crack down on tax payments.
newsitem.headline: Detroit mayor calls for crack down on tax payments.

text.p: Detroit Mayor Dennis Archer outlined a plan to crack down on income tax collections in his state of the city address Tuesday evening.

The mayor said the city would gain between $29 million and $39 million in uncollected taxes within three years by tracking down non-filers, particularly non-residents, and processing returns and collecting revenues more effectively.

Archer also cited the city's improved financial condition that led in October to a rating upgrade by Moody's Investors Service to Baa from Ba1. Fitch Investors Service also upgraded its rating that month to BBB from BBB-minus. And, Standard & Poor's Corp. changed its outlook on Detroit's rating to positive from stable.

"By building a deficit-free budget, we say to everyone, including Wall Street, potential investors in Detroit, and our local taxpayers, Detroit has its financial house in order," Archer said. "We manage out money well and we pay our bills."

The mayor also listed upcoming developments for the Motor City that included new stadiums for the Detroit Lions football and Detroit Tigers baseball teams, three voter-approved casinos, as well as General Motors Corp. decision to move its headquarters to the Renaissance Center in downtown Detroit.

In addition, Archer pointed out the city was acting on its designation as a federal empowerment zone and state of Michigan, tax-free Renaissance Zone, which were both aimed at bringing new development into the city.
"The state of the city tonight is better than it has been in decades," Archer said.

As for the city's school district, Archer said that Gov. John Engler's recently announced plan to allow for the state to take over academically troubled schools was extreme and only warranted "when other local attempts have failed."
